newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB sees major cost from computer bug.
newsitem.headline: NAB sees major cost from computer bug.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) said on Thursday the computer "millenium bug" would result in fairly significant costs for the bank, but also presented an opportunity for the standardisation of its worldwide network.
"It's a fairly significant investment that we'll need to make to correct that (the millenium bug)," NAB spokesman Haydn Park told Reuters.
"We'll probably take that as an opportunity to standardise our computer network around the world, so there's always a positive."
The millenium bug is a worldwide programming problem that will cause computers to view the year 2000 as the year 1900.
This will occur as a result of a programming fault which only allows computers to accept the last two digits of a year.
As a result, companies will have to re-programme their computers to accept a four-digit field before 2000 in order to avoid computer chaos.
Managing director Don Argus said earlier the bank was in the process of costing the re-programming of its computers and hoped to make an announcement about that soon.
"We're in the process of getting the whole thing mapped and planned out and obviously, costed," Argus told reporters.
"I'll be able to make some further announcements about that later on, but I'd say there will be an investment required around the group and it won't be insignificant."
NAB earlier announced a 14.1 percent rise in first half net profit to A$1.14 billion, which was within market expectations.
